newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnamese-Canadian faces trial for life in Hanoi.
newsitem.headline: Vietnamese-Canadian faces trial for life in Hanoi.

text.p: A Vietnamese Canadian woman will go on trial for her life later this week on charges of trafficking in heroin, a diplomat at Ottawa's embassy in Hanoi said on Tuesday.
The diplomat said Nguyen Thi Hiep, 40, would face a Hanoi court on Friday. It was not clear whether embassy officials or foreign journalists would be allowed to attend.
Hiep and her mother were arrested in April last year at Hanoi's Noi Bai airport as they checked in for a flight to Hong Kong.
Customs officials were reported to have found 5.4 kg (11.9 lb) of heroin, packed in small bags and hidden behind five lacquerware paintings in their luggage.
Vietnamese state media said Hiep's mother, Tran Thi Cam, who is in her 70s, would also face trial.
The diplomat was unable to confirm this.
Sentences for drug-trafficking in Vietnam include the death penalty.

Drugs experts say the communist country is fast becoming both a market and conduit for illegal narcotics from Southeast Asia's notorious Golden Triangle producing area, which straddles the borders of Laos, Burma and Thailand.
